stories.title: Integrate GA4 analytics via @next/third-parties/google
stories.description: The site has a CookieConsent component but zero analytics tracking code. Without GA4, there is no visibility into traffic sources, booking funnel drop-off, or blog performance. The @next/third-parties/google package provides a Next.js-native GoogleAnalytics component that defers loading until after hydration for performance.
acceptanceCriteria: GoogleAnalytics component with measurement ID added to root layout.tsx, gated behind cookie consent
sendGAEvent helper used for at minimum: 'book_click', 'whatsapp_click', and blog page views
GA4 script does NOT load before the user accepts cookie consent (PDPA/GDPR)
Google Tag Assistant confirms events are received in debug view
technicalNotes: Use @next/third-parties/google — official package, no extra bundle weight
Ref: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/next-script-for-ga
CookieConsent.tsx already exists — wire the consent callback to conditionally render <GoogleAnalytics />
Measurement ID format: G-XXXXXXXXXX from GA4 property settings

stories.title: Add App Router error boundaries: error.tsx and global-error.tsx
stories.description: The Next.js App Router requires explicit error.tsx files per route segment for graceful error handling. Currently the site has no error boundaries — a runtime error on any page results in a blank screen with no user guidance. global-error.tsx is the last-resort fallback that replaces the root layout on catastrophic errors.
acceptanceCriteria: src/app/error.tsx created with a branded fallback UI and a 'Try again' reset button
src/app/global-error.tsx created with its own <html> and <body> tags as required by Next.js
Error component calls reset() prop when user clicks retry
Error page matches hostel branding (not default Next.js error page)
Accessing a broken route in production shows the custom error UI, not a blank page
technicalNotes: error.tsx receives { error: Error, reset: () => void } props
global-error.tsx must include <html> and <body> as it replaces root layout
In development an overlay is shown instead; test in production build (npm run build && npm start)
Ref: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling

stories.title: Remove duplicate public/robots.txt — rely solely on robots.ts
stories.description: There are two robots files: the dynamic src/app/robots.ts (Next.js App Router convention) and a static public/robots.txt. The static file in /public takes precedence over the dynamically generated one, meaning the App Router robots.ts is silently ignored. This is a technical SEO inconsistency that prevents the sitemap URL from being properly advertised.
acceptanceCriteria: public/robots.txt file is archived (not permanently deleted per project policy)
GET /robots.txt returns the correct response generated by src/app/robots.ts
Sitemap URL in robots output matches https://pelangicapsulehostel.com/sitemap.xml
Google Search Console 'Robots.txt' report shows no errors after deploy
technicalNotes: Next.js App Router: src/app/robots.ts generates /robots.txt at request time
Files in /public are served as-is and override App Router route handlers for the same path
Archive the old public/robots.txt content to 4-archive/ before removal
Ref: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots

stories.title: Add image entries to sitemap.ts for gallery and room photos
stories.description: sitemap.ts generates page URLs but contains no image entries. Google's image sitemap extension allows crawlers to discover gallery images, room photos, and hero images — critical for a hostel whose visual appeal drives bookings. This is especially important since Next.js lazy-loads images that Googlebot may not execute scripts to find.
acceptanceCriteria: Gallery page sitemap entry includes an images[] array with all /images/*.webp URLs and descriptive captions
Rooms page entry includes capsule pod images with captions
Homepage entry includes hero image
Each image entry has url, title, and caption fields as per Google image sitemap specification
Google Search Console Image Indexing report shows increased indexed images after deploy
technicalNotes: Next.js MetadataRoute.Sitemap supports images property per entry since Next.js 14.2
Image sitemap format: { url, images: [{ url, title, caption }] }
All image URLs must be absolute (https://pelangicapsulehostel.com/images/...)
Ref: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap

stories.title: Add VideoObject schema to check-in page for YouTube embed
stories.description: The check-in page embeds a YouTube video but has no VideoObject structured data. Google uses VideoObject schema to generate video rich results and video carousels — particularly valuable for search queries like 'pelangi hostel check in' or 'capsule hostel JB how to check in', driving qualified traffic from travelers actively planning their stay.
acceptanceCriteria: VideoObject JSON-LD added to check-in page with name, description, thumbnailUrl, uploadDate, and embedUrl
thumbnailUrl uses a publicly accessible HTTPS URL at least 1200px wide
Google Rich Results Test validates the VideoObject without errors
Schema does not duplicate or conflict with page's existing Metadata
technicalNotes: Required Google fields: name, description, thumbnailUrl, uploadDate
Recommended: duration (ISO 8601, e.g. PT3M20S), contentUrl or embedUrl
YouTube thumbnail: https://img.youtube.com/vi/6Ux11oBZaQQ/maxresdefault.jpg
Ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/video

stories.title: Add Event schema to CommunityEvents component
stories.description: CommunityEvents.tsx renders hostel events but has no Event structured data. Google surfaces events in search results and Google Events, driving incremental traffic from travelers planning a visit to JB. Events appearing in Google's event rich results significantly increase click-through rates for local and travel queries.
acceptanceCriteria: Each event in events.ts data includes startDate, endDate, location, and description fields
CommunityEvents component emits Event JSON-LD for each upcoming event
Event schema includes organizer (Pelangi Capsule Hostel), location (PostalAddress), and eventStatus
Google Rich Results Test validates Event schema without errors
Past events are excluded from schema output (only future/ongoing events emitted)
technicalNotes: Required fields: name, startDate, location (Place or PostalAddress)
Recommended: endDate, description, image, organizer, eventAttendanceMode
EventAttendanceMode: https://schema.org/OfflineEventAttendanceMode for in-person events
Ref: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event

stories.title: Add schema.org Review markup to Reviews and Testimonials components
stories.description: Reviews.tsx and Testimonials.tsx display guest reviews as HTML but emit no structured data. Individual Review items with schema.org markup help Google understand review sentiment and attribute content correctly, improving E-E-A-T signals. The existing AggregateRating has correctly been removed; adding only Review items (not AggregateRating) is safe and compliant.
acceptanceCriteria: Each testimonial/review item wrapped in schema.org Review JSON-LD with reviewBody, author (Person type), and reviewRating
Source platform (Google, Hostelworld, Booking.com) included as author.sameAs where available
Schema does not include AggregateRating (must remain absent per US-026 decision)
Google Rich Results Test shows no warnings for the Review markup
Reviews include datePublished where date is known
technicalNotes: Use @type: Review, reviewRating: { @type: Rating, ratingValue, bestRating: 5 }
Author: { @type: Person, name: '...' }
itemReviewed should reference the Hostel schema entity via @id
Ref: https://schema.org/Review

stories.title: Add ImageGallery and ImageObject schema to Gallery page
stories.description: The /gallery page has no structured data. Adding ImageGallery schema with individual ImageObject entries enables Google Image Search rich results and increases photo discoverability. For a hostel, gallery photos are the primary conversion asset — surfacing them in image search drives qualified visitors who are visually evaluating accommodation options.
acceptanceCriteria: Gallery page emits ImageGallery JSON-LD containing an array of ImageObject entries
Each ImageObject includes contentUrl, name (descriptive caption), description, and encodingFormat (image/webp)
All contentUrl values are absolute HTTPS URLs
Google Rich Results Test validates without errors
At least 6 key images (pods, common areas, exterior) included in schema
technicalNotes: Schema: { @type: ImageGallery, image: [{ @type: ImageObject, contentUrl, name, ... }] }
Absolute URLs required for all contentUrl values
Ref: https://schema.org/ImageGallery and https://schema.org/ImageObject
Ref: https://koanthic.com/en/image-schema-markup-complete-implementation-guide-2026/

stories.title: Implement Sentry error monitoring for client, server, and edge
stories.description: Production errors are currently silent — there is no error monitoring configured. Without Sentry, broken pages go undetected until a guest reports them. For a live hostel booking site, undetected booking form errors or API failures directly cost revenue. Sentry's Next.js SDK instruments client, server, and Edge Runtime with a single setup wizard.
acceptanceCriteria: @sentry/nextjs installed and initialised via Sentry wizard (npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs)
sentry.client.config.ts, sentry.server.config.ts present
withSentryConfig wrapper applied in next.config.ts
Source maps uploaded to Sentry on build via SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable
A test error triggers an issue in the Sentry project dashboard
DSN stored in NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN env var, not hardcoded
technicalNotes: Run: npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs
Set tracesSampleRate: 0.1 (10%) in production to control costs
Configure ignoreErrors for known non-actionable browser errors (ResizeObserver, etc.)
Ref: https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/

stories.title: Replace eager YouTube iframe with facade pattern on check-in page
stories.description: The check-in page loads the YouTube iframe eagerly, triggering third-party requests on every page load regardless of whether the user watches the video. A facade pattern (poster image + play overlay) defers the iframe until click, reducing initial payload by 500KB+, improving LCP, and reducing unnecessary data transfer for mobile visitors on slower connections.
acceptanceCriteria: YouTube iframe is not loaded until user clicks the play button
Thumbnail image shown as poster (fetched from YouTube's CDN at build time or statically)
Play button overlay is keyboard-accessible (focusable, activates on Enter/Space)
Play overlay meets WCAG 2.2 Target Size minimum (≥24×24px)
After click, iframe loads and autoplays correctly
Lighthouse Performance score maintains or improves vs current baseline
technicalNotes: Thumbnail URL: https://img.youtube.com/vi/6Ux11oBZaQQ/hqdefault.jpg
Pattern: useState(false) → show poster image with button → on click setState(true) → render iframe
Mark the poster image as Next.js <Image> with loading='eager' since it IS the LCP for that section
Ref: https://web.dev/third-party-facades/

stories.title: Fix WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 — Focus Not Obscured by sticky MobileBookingBar
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 (Level AA) requires keyboard-focused components are not entirely hidden by sticky UI. The MobileBookingBar is fixed at the viewport bottom. When users tab through footer links, booking CTAs, or cookie consent — elements near the bottom — the focused element may be completely hidden behind the bar, blocking keyboard navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: All focusable elements on every page are at least partially visible when focused, even with MobileBookingBar visible
scroll-padding-bottom CSS applied to html or body matching bar height (~64px) on mobile viewports
Keyboard-only navigation test passes through all pages with no fully-obscured focus indicators
WAVE accessibility tool reports no Focus Not Obscured violations on any page
Fix does not break existing scroll behaviour for mouse users
technicalNotes: Fix: add scroll-padding-bottom: 4rem (64px) to html in globals.css, scoped to mobile only via @media
Alternatively use scroll-margin-bottom on interactive elements if global fix causes side effects
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11 Level AA: component does not need to be fully visible, only partially visible
Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html

stories.title: Audit and remediate touch target sizes for WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) at Level AA requires interactive elements to have a minimum target size of 24×24 CSS pixels. The site has several candidates that may fall below this threshold: social media icon links in the Footer, blog category filter chips, and star rating icons. Failing this criterion can trigger legal accessibility complaints in EU (EAA) and US (ADA) contexts.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive elements have a touch target of at least 24×24px (target size or spacing offset)
Footer social media icon links have min-h-6 min-w-6 (24px) applied
BlogFilter category chips have min height of 24px
No clickable element smaller than 24×24px without sufficient spacing to adjacent targets
DevTools mobile emulation confirms all targets pass the 24×24px threshold
technicalNotes: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Level AA: 24×24px minimum target size OR 24px offset spacing around smaller targets
Use Tailwind min-h-6 min-w-6 (= 24px) as the minimum baseline for all interactive elements
Check: Footer social icons, BlogFilter.tsx chips, any icon-only buttons
Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html

stories.title: Add resource hints (preconnect/dns-prefetch) for third-party origins
stories.description: The site makes requests to YouTube (check-in video), Google Maps (LocationMap iframe), and TripCDN (review images) without preconnect hints. Without these hints the browser pays a full DNS + TCP + TLS round-trip penalty on first use of each origin, increasing perceived load time. Preconnect for hot paths and dns-prefetch for cold paths reduce this overhead.
acceptanceCriteria: layout.tsx includes preconnect for https://www.youtube.com and https://www.google.com
dns-prefetch added for https://ak-d.tripcdn.com
Preconnect tags appear in <head> before any resource from those origins is requested
Lighthouse 'Preconnect to required origins' audit passes with no warnings
No CORS errors in browser console related to preconnect hints
technicalNotes: Add via Next.js metadata or directly in layout.tsx <head> using next/head
Use only 2-3 preconnect hints — too many compete for connections
Pair preconnect with crossOrigin='anonymous' for font/image origins
Ref: https://web.dev/preconnect-and-dns-prefetch/

stories.title: Add email newsletter capture form for guest re-marketing
stories.description: The site has no mechanism to capture visitor emails. Email is a proven re-marketing channel for hospitality — visitors who don't book immediately can be nurtured via a newsletter (local tips, JB updates, promotions). A lightweight inline signup form placed at the bottom of the blog index converts reader intent into a direct communication channel without requiring OTA commission.
acceptanceCriteria: Newsletter signup form added to blog index page bottom with name and email fields
Form connects to an email marketing service (Brevo/Mailchimp) via a server action or API route to avoid CSP violations
Success confirmation message shown on submit
Privacy note included: 'No spam. Unsubscribe anytime.'
Form has visible labels (not placeholder-only) per WCAG 1.3.1
CookieConsent updated to mention email marketing if applicable under PDPA
technicalNotes: Brevo (Sendinblue) free tier: 300 emails/day, unlimited contacts
Use a Next.js Server Action to call Brevo API — avoids adding external script to CSP
PDPA (Malaysia): requires explicit consent before adding to mailing list
Ref: https://developers.brevo.com/reference/createcontact

stories.title: Verify WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 accessible authentication in booking flow
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 (Accessible Authentication, Minimum — Level AA) requires authentication and form processes not rely on cognitive tests (e.g., image CAPTCHA) as the only option. The /book page proxies an external SPA from admin.pelangicapsulehostel.com — this remote booking form must be verified to support password managers, not block paste, and offer accessible auth alternatives if any CAPTCHA is present.
acceptanceCriteria: Booking SPA at /book supports password manager autofill (no autocomplete='off' on credential fields)
No field blocks paste operations (no onPaste preventDefault on any input)
If CAPTCHA is present in booking flow, at least one accessible alternative is offered
Contact form (if added in future) follows same rules
Test with screen reader confirms no authentication barriers in booking flow
technicalNotes: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 Level AA — new in WCAG 2.2, referenced in EAA (EU effective 2025) and ADA (US)
The proxied /book SPA (admin.pelangicapsulehostel.com) must also comply — coordinate with admin site
Ensure all <input> elements have appropriate autocomplete attributes
Ref: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum.html
